Description
	 
		(last modified by Jonny Fuller)
	 
Hi friends,
During testing I discovered a strange bug when using a query expression for ordering during multi-table inheritance. You can find the full write up as well as reproducible test repository ​https://github.com/JonnyWaffles/djangoordermetabug. The bug occurs because the field is an OrderBy object, not a string, during get_order_dir. The linked stacktrace should make the issue obvious, but what I don't understand is why it only fails during test db setup, not during repl or script use. I wish I could help more and come up with a real solution. Hopefully, this is enough for someone wiser to find the culprit.

Now I see the issue. In `find_ordering_name`, at line ~725, when a field is a relation and opts.ordering contains expressions (like `OrderBy` objects), the code recursively calls `self.find_ordering_name(item, opts, alias, order, already_seen)` for each item in `opts.ordering`. But `find_ordering_name` calls `get_order_dir(name, default_order)` which expects a string, not an expression object.

The fix should handle the case where `item` in `opts.ordering` is an expression (has `resolve_expression`). When iterating over `opts.ordering` items, if the item is an expression, it should be handled differently rather than being passed to `find_ordering_name` which expects a string.
